module_title: Supreme Court - Jurisdictions and Removal Process
introduction: At this level, we focus on the various types of jurisdictions (powers) the Supreme Court holds and the rigorous process required to remove a judge, ensuring judicial independence.

core_concepts.title: Original Jurisdiction (Article 131)
core_concepts.description: The SC decides disputes between: 1. Centre vs. one or more States. 2. Centre and any State(s) vs. other State(s). 3. Between two or more States.

core_concepts.title: Writ Jurisdiction (Article 32)
core_concepts.description: The SC is the protector of Fundamental Rights. It can issue 5 types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari.

core_concepts.title: Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143)
core_concepts.description: The President can seek the opinion of the SC on any question of law or fact of public importance. The SC's opinion is NOT binding on the President.

core_concepts.title: Court of Record (Article 129)
core_concepts.description: The judgments of the SC are recorded for perpetual memory and testimony. They are legally binding on all lower courts. It also has the power to punish for its own contempt.

core_concepts.title: Removal of Judges
core_concepts.description: A judge can be removed by the President only after an address by Parliament, supported by a special majority (2/3rd members present and voting + majority of total strength) on grounds of 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity'.

important_entities.name: The Collegium System
important_entities.significance: A body of the CJI and 4 senior-most judges that recommends names for appointment. It evolved through the 'Three Judges Cases'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Disputes regarding inter-state river waters are EXCLUDED from the Original Jurisdiction of the SC; Parliament creates separate tribunals for them.
The SC's writ jurisdiction is narrower than High Courts because the SC can only issue writs for 'Fundamental Rights', whereas HCs can issue them for 'any other purpose' as well.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A simple way to categorize the major powers of the Supreme Court.

exam_strategy_tips: Article 143 (Advisory) and Article 129 (Court of Record) are high-yield articles for competitive exams.
No judge of the Supreme Court has been impeached so far, though proceedings were initiated against some.
